column3: The Hebrew names messengers rather than kings and says the year returned, without an explicit spring or march “to war.” It says all Israel, without a separate noun “army.”
The Hebrew explicitly calls the building the king’s house; BSB uses “palace.”
The Hebrew gives the reply as an active singular saying and a negative question, “Is this not...?” BSB uses a passive report and a statement.
The Hebrew actively says David took her and describes her purification with a participle; BSB makes taking the messengers’ purpose and renders the purification as recently completed.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew repeats Uriah’s name in Joab’s sending; BSB uses “him.”
The Hebrew repeats the welfare term separately for Joab, the people, and the battle; BSB combines these inquiries.
The Hebrew explicitly names David as speaker; BSB uses “he.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew actively says unnamed people told David and repeats the downward movement twice; BSB uses a passive report and “go home.”
The Hebrew explicitly names David as Uriah’s audience and calls Joab’s companions “my lord’s servants”; BSB leaves the audience implicit and uses “his soldiers.”
The Hebrew says “also today” and “send you”; BSB has “one more day” and adds “back.”
The Hebrew names neither Uriah nor David in the later clauses and says he ate “before him”; BSB repeatedly names Uriah and has “with him.”
The Hebrew explicitly names Uriah’s hand in sending the letter; BSB uses “with Uriah.”
The Hebrew expresses the striking passively and the dying actively; BSB uses passive “struck down and killed.”
The Hebrew says Joab knew valiant men were there; BSB says he saw “the strongest enemy soldiers.”
The Hebrew explicitly identifies the fallen as some of the people, some of David’s servants; BSB condenses the group.
The Hebrew uses separate sending and reporting verbs; BSB combines this as sending an account.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew uses an ordinary saying verb where BSB has asking, and explicitly names the king’s anger as rising.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew separately says the messenger went and came; BSB condenses the movement as setting out.
The Hebrew says they were against the enemy up to the gate; BSB makes driving them back explicit.
The Hebrew says some servants died with an active dying verb; BSB has passive “were killed.”
The Hebrew retains the eyes image in the warning about the matter and does not explicitly say “with these words” in the final encouragement.
The Hebrew repeats Uriah’s name when reporting his death and calls him her husband again; BSB uses pronouns.
The Hebrew explicitly says David sent and gathered her into his house; BSB condenses this as having her brought.
